sections.title: Next steps on dishes she already makes
sections.intro: Same flavors she likes, made a slightly new way.

sections.title: More Tex-Mex
sections.intro: About 25 of her meals are Tex-Mex. These add new ways to use the toppings she already buys.

sections.title: Takeout she could make herself
sections.intro: Things she has ordered and photographed. Each one uses skills she has already shown.

sections.title: More weeknight dinners
sections.intro: A second round, picked to cover more proteins. Each one takes about 40 minutes or less.

sections.title: Slow cooker
sections.intro: She already uses a slow cooker (a soup on Dec 2, 2024). These take about 20 minutes of prep, then cook on their own. The birria tacos in the Tex-Mex section are also slow-cooker recipes.

sections.title: Warm and cozy
sections.intro: Four new recipes for crisp fall days. The "Warm & cozy" filter also finds the soups, stews, bakes and slow-cooker dishes elsewhere on the page, including ones she has already made.

sections.title: Pasta & Italian
sections.intro: Her biggest category. These are my versions of what's in the photos, not her exact recipes. Cards marked Likely or Best guess are the ones I'm less sure about.

box.blurb: Three poke bowls this month (Oct 13–16, 2026) and salmon over rice with scallions five times (March 2025, August 2026). This is the same idea, baked as a casserole.
She already sears tuna: sliced over avocado and cucumber (Feb 2025), sesame-crusted (Mar 30, 2026), and in the October bowls. Crispy rice adds crunch.
Pasta is her biggest category. She makes both red sauce (rigatoni, Jul 2024; pappardelle, Aug 2026) and cream sauce (shrimp alfredo, Sep 2024). Vodka sauce is both at once.
Eggs are her most common breakfast, she made a tomato and egg scramble (Aug 13, 2025), and garlic toast is her usual side.
She's made loaded potatoes about eight times (bacon, sour cream and scallions in Oct 2025; buffalo chicken in Nov 2024) and a sweet potato with ground beef (Jul 21, 2026).
She made a sliced chicken bowl with peppers, corn and black beans (May 18, 2026) and steak tacos (Nov 18, 2025). This makes the filling on one pan.
She uses a slow cooker (Dec 2, 2024), makes beef stew (Oct 2025, Mar 2026) and steak tacos. These are cheesy, crispy tacos you dip in their own broth.
She ordered pad see ew (Aug 21, 2025) and pad thai (Dec 15, 2024), and she already makes chicken and broccoli stir-fry (Jan 2025).
She makes egg fried rice in a skillet (Mar 3, 2026), ordered hibachi (Sep 14, 2024), and puts a mayo sauce on all her bowls.
She has eaten Ethiopian food twice (Aug 30, 2025 and Aug 29, 2026). Red lentils are cheap and the dish keeps for days.
She bought a Chipotle bowl (May 27, 2026), and she builds her own bowls more than anything else.
She has posted runny eggs on toast at least six times (Sep 2024 to Aug 2025), often with avocado and hot sauce. This puts the eggs on garlicky yogurt with chili butter.
Chia with blueberries and pepitas (Sep 27, 2026) and chocolate chia with raspberries (Sep 16, 2026). A fall flavor using the same method.
She has posted yogurt, granola and blueberry bowls many times (Jan 31 and Feb 3, 2026) and made a lemon dessert (Nov 11, 2024). One pan covers breakfast for several days.
A combination of her squash soup (Sep 23, 2026) and her cheesy sausage-and-pepper pasta (Sep 28, 2026).
The squash soup she already makes, with Thai flavors like the takeout she orders.
Ground beef is the meat she cooks most (taco meat, taco salads, lettuce wraps on Mar 2, 2026), and rice bowls with scallions and a mayo drizzle are her favorite format.
She has made salmon over rice with scallions five times (March 2025, August 2026). A sweet-salty glaze is an easy change from her usual.
She made a creamy chicken and spinach pasta (Nov 6, 2025) and finishes nearly everything with parmesan. This is the same sauce with sun-dried tomatoes.
She roasted a pork tenderloin and served it with green beans in spring 2025, and blistered green beans or asparagus show up with a lot of her dinners. This version cooks everything on one pan.
She has made shrimp alfredo (Sep 25, 2024) and shrimp with ravioli (July 2024), plus a creamy orzo with broccoli. This combines the shrimp and the orzo.
She has posted burritos with tater tots (spring 2026) and an egg-and-tots plate (this past winter). These put everything in one wrap that keeps in the freezer.
She makes pasta salads (a caprese one in August 2025) and cowboy caviar (Sep 16, 2026). This brings Mexican street-corn flavors to a pasta salad.
Chicken goes into a lot of her Tex-Mex meals, like the chicken and black bean bowl (May 18, 2026). One batch makes enough for bowls, tacos and quesadillas all week.
Her tacos and burrito bowls (steak tacos Nov 18, 2025; a Chipotle bowl May 27, 2026) are a natural fit for carnitas, and a quick broil makes the pork crispy.
She posted chili with avocado, sour cream and cilantro, with cornbread on the side, on Oct 7, 2026. A slow-cooker batch covers several dinners.
She makes a lot of tomato-cream sauces and a lot of dinners over rice. This is a new flavor in that same style.
She makes chicken and broccoli stir-fries (Jan 24, 2025) and orders takeout often. This is a takeout classic that cooks while she's out.
She made beef stew with white beans (Oct 29, 2025) and often serves soup with garlic toast and parmesan. This is a lighter Italian-style soup.
Her corn chowder (Dec 3, 2025) and slow-cooker soup (Dec 2, 2024) show she likes a creamy, hearty bowl. This is pot pie in soup form.
She roasted pork tenderloin twice in June 2025 and made squash soup on Sep 23, 2026. This puts fall flavors on a weeknight pork dinner.
Red-sauce pasta is her most-posted dish, and she has made sausage and pepper pasta three times. This bakes them together under melted cheese.
She made cinnamon rolls (Jul 29, 2024) and frosted bars for Thanksgiving (Nov 27, 2025). These are her rolls with pumpkin in the dough.
Rigatoni or spaghetti in red sauce under grated parmesan, usually with garlic toast.
Wide ribbon pasta in a meaty tomato sauce with shaved parmesan and basil.
Browned meatballs in marinara over spaghetti with lots of parmesan.
